restatements.text: Defines terms used in the measure, including applicable individual, applicable trust, net worth, related person, and valuation dates.
Authorizes the Franchise Tax Board to issue regulations, exempts its rulemaking from the Administrative Procedure Act until 2028, and sets a 10-year window to mail deficiency assessments for 2026.
Permits the Legislature to amend the Act by a two-thirds vote, provided the amendment is consistent with and furthers the Act's purposes.
Declares the Act's provisions severable and directs courts to reform dates if applying the tax retrospectively is found unconstitutional.

Establishes financial penalties for tax understatements, authorizes the Franchise Tax Board to disregard transactions lacking economic substance, allows the Board to hire outside experts, and permits the Board to seek a trial de novo if it disagrees with the Office of Tax Appeals.
States the Act shall be liberally construed.
Sets a 60-day window for filing an expedited validation action in Sacramento County Superior Court to resolve the Act's facial validity, with direct appeal to the California Supreme Court.
Prohibits taxpayers from claiming a state income tax deduction for the wealth tax paid under this Act.
Provides that if another wealth tax measure appears on the same ballot, this measure supersedes it entirely if this measure receives more affirmative votes.

Grants the State, proponents, or any citizen standing to sue or intervene to defend the Act's legality in court, and requires the State to pay reasonable legal fees and costs for defending the Act if the Attorney General does not.

evidence.quote: the Board may distribute, apportion, or allocate assets, liabilities, or any other items relevant to the determination of net worth under this Part between or among such persons if the Board determines that such distribution, apportionment, or allocation is necessary in order to prevent avoidance of the tax imposed by this Part
evidence.why: It increases complexity by allowing the tax board to retroactively reallocate assets and disregard entities to determine a taxpayer's actual net worth.

evidence.quote: No deduction shall be allowed for any tax imposed by the State on net worth, including the 2026 Billionaire Tax Act (Part 27 of this Code) notwithstanding any other provision of law
evidence.why: It prevents individuals paying the billionaire wealth tax from deducting it from their state income taxes, ensuring they bear the full cost of the new tax.

evidence.quote: every notice of a proposed deficiency assessment under this part in regards to taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026, and before January 1, 2027, shall be mailed to the taxpayer within ten years after the return was filed.
evidence.why: It increases the state's enforcement capacity by granting the tax board a ten-year window to issue deficiency assessments for the 2026 tax year.

evidence.quote: The penalty under this Section for a gross understatement of tax shall be an amount equal to 40 percent of any understatement of tax.
evidence.why: It increases enforcement powers by levying substantial financial penalties for understating tax liability.

evidence.quote: Until January 1, 2028, the rulemaking provisions of the Administrative Procedure Act (Chapter 3.5 (commencing with Section 11340) of Part 1 of Division 3 of Title 2 of the Government Code) shall not apply to any regulation, standard, criterion, procedure, determination, rule, notice, guideline, or any other guidance established or issued by the Board pursuant to this Part.
evidence.why: It expands the regulatory powers of the Franchise Tax Board by exempting its rules and guidance from standard administrative procedures.

evidence.quote: If the Board determines that a transaction or series of transactions lack economic substance, or that a substantial purpose for any transaction or series of transactions was to obtain a tax benefit with respect to this Part that is not intended by the voters or the Legislature, the Board may determine the tax consequences to any person in a manner that is reasonable in light of all the facts and circumstances in order to deny such benefit.
evidence.why: It increases agency power by allowing the tax board to disregard specific transactions or entities it determines lack economic substance.

evidence.why: It strengthens citizens' initiative powers by guaranteeing proponents and citizens the legal standing and public funding to defend their successful initiative in court.

evidence.why: It expands the regulatory powers of the tax board by removing standard rulemaking requirements for a temporary period.

evidence.why: It creates broad new powers for the tax board to investigate and override the stated form of transactions based on economic substance doctrines.

analysis.answer: Current law is not provided. The measure establishes rules for a new wealth tax, exempts the Franchise Tax Board from standard administrative procedure requirements for two years, and extends the statute of limitations for mailing deficiency assessments for the 2026 tax year to ten years.

Current law is not provided. The measure explicitly creates standing for the proponent or any citizen to sue or intervene to defend the law, and mandates that the state bear the reasonable fees and costs of defending it if the Attorney General declines to do so.

Direct costs include administration, the expense of hiring outside experts and counsel, and court resources to handle trial de novo proceedings. Opportunity costs include heavy compliance and legal burdens for taxpayers attempting to value assets and navigate complex anti-avoidance regulations.
The state faces direct, potentially unbudgeted costs to pay the legal fees of proponents or citizens intervening to defend the Act if the Attorney General does not.

Billionaires and complex entities will bear the compliance costs and tax burden. The Franchise Tax Board benefits from expanded discretion, extended enforcement windows, and the ability to employ outside counsel.

Taxpayers are strongly incentivized to avoid aggressive undervaluation schemes due to the massive 40 percent penalty on gross understatements and the broad authority given to the tax board to ignore transactions lacking economic substance.

The Franchise Tax Board gains extraordinary discretion and power, particularly through exemptions from standard rulemaking, an extended 10-year audit window, and the ability to request a trial de novo. Citizens and initiative proponents gain the power to legally intervene and defend the law at state expense.

The measure is statutory but locks in its provisions by requiring a two-thirds supermajority vote of the Legislature to amend it, and restricting amendments to only those that further the purposes of the Act.
